name: Effektiv Spenden (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Moves money: each recipient its donors give to, read live, brings its own countries.
summary: Effektiv Spenden runs a donation platform for Germany, Switzerland and Austria that passes tax-deductible gifts on to charities recommended by evaluators, with its own funds and donor advice; this model covers all its spending in 2025 ($1.34M across its German, Swiss and Austrian entities). At the defaults it averts about 24 years of healthy life per $1,000: of the $32M donors gave through it, its own donor survey suggests it caused about 31% (giving that would not have happened or would have gone to an ordinary charity), which with the gifts its advice steered comes to about $11M, eight dollars per dollar it spends, each dollar valued at the causes its donors chose (48% to fighting poverty, mostly GiveWell's charities; climate, animal welfare, catastrophic risks and democracy at the site's figures for their recipients), half of the platform giving counted as new money and the advised gifts only for the gain over where they would have gone, after the wait for its funds' half-yearly grants, and the next dollar at 32% of the past average. It moves about eight dollars, half of it to top global-health charities, for each dollar it spends. The result moves most with its next-dollar figure, the discount rate, how far its survey's non-respondents were influenced and where shifted money would otherwise have gone; only the advised gifts are discounted for missing data, since what its advice changed is judged; platform money is counted.

sections.title: Adjustments
sections.explainer: Discounts for weaker evidence, what would have happened anyway, credit shared with others, and delivery falling short. All multiply the outcome.

sections.title: Career changes
sections.explainer: People the charity moves into high-impact jobs: per career changed, the pay they give up for the years they stay, valued at the new employer's live result per dollar, times the share of changes the charity caused (docs/normalization.md 2.8). The mirror of staff pay below market.

sections.title: Outcome
sections.explainer: The outcome in the family's shared unit, per dollar.

sections.title: Your dollar's share
sections.explainer: Staff who earn less than they could elsewhere pay part of the cost in kind. With credit by share of resources, your dollar is credited with its share of the full cost only.

sections.title: Value of a dollar moved (shared)
sections.explainer: charityevals' shared method for money a meta charity moves, the same rows in every such model (docs/normalization.md 2.8). A dollar moved is worth what the charities it reaches achieve, each at its live result on this site under your values; new money counts in full, shifted money only for the gain over where it would have gone.

source.quote: 19% of total survey respondents did not fall into any of the three groups above and stated that they would not have donated at all without Effektiv Spenden.

rows.explainer: Its post-donation survey, 4,714 complete answers over 2019–2022. Respondents referred by partners (GiveWell, Giving What We Can, the charities) or very familiar with effective giving count as caused by nothing, even when they said they would not have given: a cautious classification.

rows.label: Surveyed donors who would otherwise have given to another, non-recommended charity

source.title: Effektiv Spenden, The Giving Multiplier for Effektiv Spenden 2019–2022 (impact evaluation, December 2023)
source.quote: This last group makes up 47% of survey respondents.

rows.explainer: Their giving was redirected by Effektiv Spenden: caused by it, as shifted money (the shared rows below credit only the gain over an ordinary charity). The other 34% would have given to the same or other recommended charities anyway, or came through partners.

rows.label: Share of donations whose donors answered the survey
rows.explainer: Our judgment, anchored on its own donor counts: 4,714 complete answers over 2019–2022, when it had more than 9,000 donors in 2021 alone (its review of that year), about 12,000 in 2024 (Jahresrückblick 2024) and far fewer in 2019–2020 (donations of €2.84M in 2020 against €18.86M in 2021); our rough total of about 23,000 donor-years over 2019–2022 puts the answers at about a fifth of donors. Many give several times a year and answers are not weighted by gift size, so the share of donations covered may be lower or higher. Its evaluation gives no response rate. 20% (8% to 40%).

rows.label: Survey answer to own effect: non-respondents counted at the shared share of respondents' influence
rows.explainer: The shared rule for an organisation's own donor survey: those who didn't answer are less engaged, influenced at half the respondents' rate (a quarter to all). Its evaluation made no non-response adjustment.

source.quote: Ein Drittel des Spendenvolumens in 2024 kam von unseren Großspenderinnen und Großspendern (0,2%), die jeweils über 100.000 € gespendet haben.

rows.explainer: 2024, the latest year it gives the split. The survey counts each respondent once, whatever they give, so the large donors' influence is weighted below by their share of the money.

rows.label: Effektiv Spenden's influence on its largest donors, as a share of its influence on the others
rows.explainer: Our judgment: donors giving over €100,000 are mostly already committed effective givers using it for tax-deductible gifts abroad. Anchored on Giving What We Can's surveys, where its major pledgers' counterfactual share was 13.7% against 37.3% for others (0.37), and its evaluation counting donor-years over $140,000 at none; 30% (5% to 70%).

rows.label: Share of platform donations that Effektiv Spenden caused (new or redirected)
rows.explainer: Its own effect (the shared rule, facts/meta.json own_effect_share: the organisation's own donor survey where it has one): the respondents who would not have given or would have given elsewhere (66%), non-respondents at the shared share, large gifts at their lower influence. About 31%, beside its own best guess of 32% (which also folds in how much better the recommended charities are, a step the shared rows take here). The survey is from 2019–2022, three years before the money counted.

rows.label: Platform donations Effektiv Spenden caused, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Donations for charities net of what donors would have given to the same effective charities anyway.

rows.label: Donations its advice steered straight to recommended charities, 2025 (€)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, anchored on its 2024 figure: 'rund 3 Mio. € an Spenden durch unsere Beratung beeinflussen, die im Anschluss unabhängig von unserer Plattform direkt an hochwirksame Organisationen gingen' (Jahresrückblick 2024); it gives no 2025 figure. Its own evaluation leaves these out.

rows.label: Share of advised donations whose destination Effektiv Spenden's advice changed
rows.explainer: No survey of advised donors: the shared figure for a meta charity without one (30%, 15% to 45%), read as the share of the advised gifts its advice redirected. People who ask a giving platform for advice were giving anyway, so none of it counts as new money (templates.md: research or advice that changes where money is spent is all shifted).

rows.label: Advised donations whose destination its advice changed, 2025 (US$)
rows.explainer: Advised gifts × the share its advice changed, at the 2025 rate.

rows.label: Advised donations its advice redirected, 2025 (US$), valued as all shifted
rows.explainer: The money the shared informed_money_value row reads: advised gifts its advice redirected, given anyway, so valued only for the gain over where they would have gone, after the evidence and missing-data steps. Platform donations it caused (money_moved, about $10M) are valued separately as money moved, net of where shifted money would have gone. Its 10% Pledge (with Giving What We Can) is given through the platform and counted there, not again.

rows.label: Money moved per dollar of the charity's cost
rows.explainer: Context: platform donations it caused plus advised gifts it redirected, per dollar of its costs (about eight).

rows.label: Average time a platform donation waits before it reaches the charity (years)
rows.explainer: Our judgment: its funds allocate twice a year, so fund money waits about a quarter of a year on average plus the time to pay out, while gifts to a named charity are passed on within weeks. The year-end balances held for charities over the year's donations, (€10.97M at the start and €17.19M at the end of 2025 in Germany, UES Bilanz p. 2; CHF 3.06M and 3.17M in Switzerland, ESS Bilanz p. 2) ÷ $32M, give 0.62 years, the high end: December's giving peak inflates both balances. 0.35 years (0.1 to 0.62).

rows.label: Discount for the wait before platform donations reach the charities
rows.explainer: The wait discounted at the shared rate, like every future benefit. Advised gifts go straight to the charities, so only platform money waits.

rows.explainer: GiveWell's four Top Charities (Against Malaria Foundation, Malaria Consortium, Helen Keller Intl, New Incentives), each at GiveWell's figure for the charity on the rankings (its programmes and locations weighted by funding) under your values, weighted by what GiveWell directed to each in 2024 (50%, 29%, 18%, 4%).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, units of value
rows.explainer: Valued by where this organisation's money went: its own published split, each recipient at its live result on this site (value_destinations).

rows.label: Value of a dollar where shifted money would otherwise have gone (our judgment: 1× GiveDirectly), units of value
rows.explainer: Our judgment. Shifted money was going to be given anyway; it is credited only for the gain. Where it would have gone is valued at GiveDirectly's live result (GiveWell's model), as Ambitious Impact does, times a shared multiple (1×, from 0 to 3×).

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): the charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work.

rows.label: Value of a dollar all shifted (given anyway, now to a better use), at the mobiliser's share, units of value
rows.explainer: Money that would have been given or spent anyway counts only for the gain over where it would have gone: a grantmaker's grants, or spending that research or advice changed. Its owners spent it, so the organisation is credited its share of that gain (mobiliser_share).

rows.label: Value of the spending its research or advice changed (all shifted money), units of value
rows.explainer: Spending its research or advice changed, at a judged share of the money it informed: all of it would have been spent anyway, so it counts for the gain over where it would have gone, discounted for weak evidence and for an outcome not measured for this charity (docs/normalization.md 2.8, 2.12).

rows.label: Value of a dollar moved, net of where shifted money would have gone, at the mobiliser's share, units of value
rows.explainer: New money counts in full; shifted money counts for the gain over where it would have gone. The donors gave it, so the organisation is credited its share of that good (mobiliser_share).

rows.label: Value of a dollar to the charities Effektiv Spenden's donors gave to (its 2025 split by cause, live), units of value
rows.explainer: Where its donors' money went in 2025 by cause (Transparenz page), each cause at its recipients' figures on the rankings under your values, by the site's rule for a split (normalization.md 2.8). Within each cause two recipient lists are blended by the Swiss association's share of the 2025 money (27%), an approximation since the 2024 list already includes Swiss giving: the organisation-wide 2024 split, the latest it publishes for the whole organisation, and the Swiss association's 2025 grants by recipient (audited accounts, the only recipient-level list for 2025); in each, recipients without a model here take the average of the modelled ones in their cause. Fighting poverty (48%): 2024, its poverty fund (which follows GiveWell's All Grants Fund) at GiveWell's Top Charities (value_global_health), GiveDirectly, Malaria Consortium, Against Malaria Foundation and Deworm the World (Evidence Action's figure) by their money; Swiss 2025, Evidence Action, Helen Keller Intl, GiveDirectly, StrongMinds, Against Malaria Foundation, Malaria Consortium, New Incentives and Lafiya by their grants. Climate (21%): Clean Air Task Force (our model) is the one recipient in either list with a published model here; its fund (which follows Founders Pledge's Climate Fund), Future Cleantech Architects, the Good Food Institute, DEPLOY/US and the rest take its figure (Founders Pledge's and Giving Green's models of them are not published). Animal welfare (7%): 2024, The Humane League (ACE's figure, the one the rankings show), the one modelled recipient, its fund (which follows the EA Animal Welfare Fund) and Rethink Priorities taking its figure; Swiss 2025, The Humane League, Sinergia Animal and Wild Animal Initiative by their grants. Catastrophic risks (12%): 2024, none of its recipients (its Longview-advised funds, Safe AI Forum, Civic AI Security Program, Future Matters) has a model, so the catastrophic-risk charities on the rankings, equal weights (#cause:catastrophic-risk; money movers such as 80,000 Hours left out); Swiss 2025, METR, the one modelled recipient. Democracy (9%): none of its recipients (HateAid, CORRECTIV, Campact; from August 2025 Power for Democracies' picks) has a model, so the democracy charities on the rankings, equal weights (#cause:democracy). Meta organisations (2.4%) take the average of the rest.

rows.label: Side effects of the money moved, as a share of its value
rows.explainer: Good and harm beyond the donations counted: gifts to its recommended charities made directly by people who read its recommendations, its book and press work without asking for advice, and a German-speaking norm of giving effectively (positive); donor attention drawn from other good uses and the interest its held donations earn for its own costs rather than the charities (negative). The shared figure for these effects (facts/meta.json): {{row:moved_side_effects}} (−5% to +20%) of the modelled value; its own evaluation counts only platform donations.

rows.label: Value of the money moved (units of value)
rows.explainer: Platform donations it caused, after their wait, × the net value of a dollar moved, plus the advised gifts it redirected (all shifted, with the evidence and missing-data steps), with the side effects.

rows.explainer: Effektiv Spenden's own figure (facts/next_dollar.json): {{row:marginal_vs_past_average}} (14–66%). Its German company holds about two years of its costs in reserve after two surpluses, and Open Philanthropy covers half its costs, so a further gift for operations does less than the average dollar so far.
